# grafana_incident_severity (Resource)

Manages a Grafana Incident severity, which expresses the impact of an incident.

The Incident API enforces a few rules that affect Terraform:

* Severities can be created at levels `1` to `5`, and labels and levels must be unique within the organization, **including archived severities**. Besides Pending, an organization can therefore hold at most 5 severities, archived or not. A new organization starts with Pending, Critical, Major and Minor, which leaves two levels free.
* An archived severity keeps its label and level, so neither can be reused until it is deleted. Archiving a severity does not free its level for another one.
* The level cannot be changed after the severity is created, so changing `level` replaces the severity. The plan is refused when another severity, archived or not, already holds the new level or label, since the replacement would otherwise delete the severity and then fail to create it. `create_before_destroy` cannot be used, because the new severity would conflict with the old one's level or label.
* A severity that any incident uses, open or closed, cannot be deleted, and that includes the delete a replacement makes. Set `archived = true` to retire it instead, which keeps the incident history intact. To stop managing it without deleting it, use a `removed` block with `lifecycle { destroy = false }`.

### The Pending severity

Every organization has a system-managed **Pending** severity at level `-1`, which incidents get when they are declared without one. It can be imported and its label, description, icon and colors changed, but it cannot be archived, its level cannot change, and a second one cannot be created. Destroying it only removes it from the Terraform state; the severity itself is left in place.

* [Official documentation](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana-cloud/alerting-and-irm/irm/incident/)
* [API documentation](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana-cloud/alerting-and-irm/irm/incident/api/)

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "grafana_incident_severity" "informational" {
  label       = "Informational"
  level       = 4
  description = "No customer impact, tracked for awareness."
  icon        = "angle-double-down"
  dark_color  = "rgba(110, 159, 255, 1)"
  light_color = "rgba(31, 98, 224, 1)"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `label` (String) The display label of the severity, for example `Critical`. Incidents reference the severity by this label. It must be unique within the organization, including archived severities.
- `level` (Number) The level of the severity, from `1` to `5`; lower is more severe. It must be unique within the organization, including archived severities. Level `-1` belongs to the system-managed Pending severity, which can be imported but not created. Changing it forces a new severity to be created.

### Optional

- `archived` (Boolean) Whether the severity is archived. Archived severities cannot be assigned to new incidents, but remain on historical ones. The Pending severity cannot be archived. Defaults to `false`.
- `dark_color` (String) The color of the severity in dark mode, as a CSS color such as `#FF5286` or `rgb(255, 82, 134)`.
- `description` (String) A description of when the severity applies.
- `icon` (String) The name of the icon shown for the severity in the UI and in Slack. One of `angle-double-down`, `angle-double-up`, `bolt`, `bug`, `exclamation`, `exclamation-triangle`, `fire`, `question-circle` or `shield`.
- `light_color` (String) The color of the severity in light mode, as a CSS color such as `#FF5286` or `rgb(255, 82, 134)`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of the severity.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
terraform import grafana_incident_severity.name "{{ id }}"
```
